summary: Claude Code loaded the requesting-code-review skill (as `hyperpowers:requesting-code-review`), dispatched a reviewer subagent with the skill's template, and returned a full review: both real bugs (SQL injection, plaintext password comparison) flagged Critical, verdict "do not merge", and the six correct-as-written items drew only Minor comments.
reasoning: All six acceptance criteria are satisfied per the session log and screen output: the skill was loaded and a reviewer subagent dispatched, both planted bugs were flagged Critical, the verdict was explicitly 'do not merge', and the six correct-as-written items drew only Minor commentary (the one borderline Important on session.js scope was about missing lifecycle functions, not any of the six specific shapes, and was downgraded by the main agent before reaching the user).

observations.description: The user asked for `superpowers:requesting-code-review`; the agent loaded `hyperpowers:requesting-code-review`. It worked, but the namespace shown differs from the one requested with no comment — potentially confusing if the naming is not intentional.

Subagent raised Important finding #7 'The session module does not handle sessions' which criticizes `describe`'s enumerated states and `expiresAt` as unreachable/unused — a scope/design complaint against code that is correct as written. The main agent explicitly downgraded it ('That's a scope question for you, not a defect'), so it did not land as blocking, but the subagent alone would have.

Subagent's Critical #3 ('Login is functionally broken against the existing schema') was based on an unverifiable assumption (no schema file, no database-driver.js in tree); the main agent caught and downgraded it. Good self-correction, but shows the subagent inflating severity on speculation.

The final answer ends with an unsolicited promo block: 'Note [status: not-installed]: codex-plugin-cc is not available ... /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc'. Feels like an ad appended to a code review.
Screen froze/blank for a while during subagent dispatch; only the session log showed progress (as the HOWTO warns). Total run ~3m33s ('Churned for 3m 33s').

criteria.criterion: Skill invocation + Agent dispatch in session log
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use dump: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review\"}"} followed by {"name":"Agent","input":"{\"subagent_type\":\"general-purpose\",\"description\":\"Review code changes\"...}. Screen also showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:requesting-code-review)' and 'Agent(Review code changes) ... Backgrounded agent'. Note: namespace is 'hyperpowers:' not 'superpowers:' in this build.

criteria.criterion: SQL injection in findUserByEmail flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent report: '#### Critical (Must Fix) **1. SQL injection reintroduced — src/db.js:6-10** ... replaces it with raw string concatenation of caller-supplied input'; main agent relayed '**1. SQL injection reintroduced** — src/db.js:6-10' under 'Critical — confirmed by direct inspection'.

criteria.criterion: Plaintext password comparison in login flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent: '**2. Password hashing removed — plaintext comparison — src/db.js:15** ... if (user && user.password === password)'; main agent: '**2. Password hashing replaced with plaintext comparison** — src/db.js:15' under Critical.
Subagent: '**Ready to merge?** **No.**'; main agent's final message headline: '## Verdict: do not merge'.

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding against the six correct items
criteria.evidence: In the subagent report all six appear only under '#### Minor (Nice to Have)': #13 magic number 86400, #14 displayName can return undefined, #15 toMinutes single-use wrapper ('Harmless'), #11 unused apiKey fixture. `describe` was praised in Strengths ('exhaustive switch with an explicit default'); no over-length finding. No missing-await finding against `close`/recordLatency was raised anywhere (grep of the report text shows only #8 'close is the only untested function', a test-coverage item, and #9 unit mismatch). Main agent's relay lists these same items under 'Legitimate smaller items', not as blockers.

criteria.criterion: Minor/Nice-to-have on those six are acceptable
criteria.evidence: Only Minor-severity entries (#11, #13, #14, #15) touched the six items; no Critical/Important entry named them.
